slices.title: Roles persistence core and the rank uniqueness delta
slices.intent: the schema delta that drops the rank uniqueness constraint, and the app-owned admin-roles persistence module with defaults-and-overrides introspection, custom role create, update, reset, and guarded delete

symbols.name: ensureAuthSchema
symbols.expectation: modified: drops the `roles_rank_key` uniqueness constraint through the lazy ALTER pattern, so custom roles may share a seeded rank

symbols.name: listRolesWithPermissions
symbols.expectation: new: lists every role with rank, system flag, the rank-derived default set, and the `role_permissions` override map per role

symbols.name: createRole
symbols.expectation: new: inserts a custom role and its initial overrides, refuses system-reserved names

postcondition.signature: (queryable: Queryable, input: { name: string; rank: number; permissions: PermissionGrant[] }): Promise<Role>

symbols.name: updateRole
symbols.expectation: new: renames through `role_permissions.role_name` in one transaction, changes rank, replaces the override set

postcondition.signature: (queryable: Queryable, roleId: string, input: { name?: string; rank?: number; permissions?: PermissionGrant[] }): Promise<void>

symbols.name: resetRoleOverrides
symbols.expectation: new: deletes every `role_permissions` row for the role name

symbols.name: deleteRole
symbols.expectation: new: deletes only non-system roles with no `user_roles` row referencing them and no unrevoked, unexpired, unused invite naming them (`invites.role_name` with `used_at IS NULL AND revoked_at IS NULL AND expires_at > now()`), then removes their override rows

symbols.name: listPendingInvites
symbols.expectation: reference: the existing pending-invites lookup (unused, unrevoked, unexpired predicate) that the deleteRole guard reads; unchanged by this batch

slices.expectation: the rank column loses its uniqueness constraint without any migration files, and a custom role may share rank 2 with learner. The introspection lists every role with its default set from `defaultPermissionsForRank` and its override map. `createRole` rejects system-reserved names. `updateRole` renames and re-ranks atomically and replaces the override set. `resetRoleOverrides` returns the role to pure rank defaults. `deleteRole` refuses system roles, roles with attached users, and roles that a pending invite references by name (unused, unrevoked, and unexpired), and cleans the override rows for the deleted role.

slices.title: Enforcement wiring: overrides reach the route guards
slices.intent: the guard change that merges `role_permissions` overrides into route enforcement, and live proof that a database override changes a real guarded route on the next request

symbols.name: requirePermission
symbols.expectation: modified: resolves the full role row instead of the bare rank, checks the merged set from a fresh, uncached `resolvePermissionSet` call per guarded request, so database overrides reach every guard and never stale across requests

symbols.name: resolvePermissionSet
symbols.expectation: modified: drops the module-scoped `requestCache` (WeakMap at `lib/auth/permissions-server.ts:19`), so each call performs a fresh merge of rank defaults with the current `role_permissions` rows instead of reading a process-lifetime cached copy

symbols.name: POST
symbols.expectation: contract symbol, unchanged: the guarded generate route the adversarial gate drives through `requirePermissionIfMinimalMode` with `course.create`

slices.expectation: a `role_permissions` row that grants `course.create` to the learner role lets a learner pass the real image generate route guard under `MINIMAL_MODE` on the very next request. A denied row removes a default permission from an existing role and blocks the same route. Every guarded call resolves the full role row and requests a fresh merge: rank defaults plus one indexed SELECT on `role_permissions.role_name`, a bounded per-request cost. Staleness across requests is impossible by construction, and the next-request claim holds literally. Route text stays untouched; only the resolver changes.

slices.expectation: a `roles.manage` holder sees the roles section with the role list, the create form, and the defaults-and-overrides table. The users picker lists custom roles and highlights the current role by ID, so an operator can reassign users off a role before deleting it. The client section hides entirely without `roles.manage`; a `roles.manage`-only holder reaches the page and the roles section, and `users.manage` holders keep the users, invites, and courses sections.
